answer: A work-weighted reputation ledger makes fake identities expensive: each agent earns weight only through attested work verified by unrelated peers, like a mesa that rises one layer at a time rather than appearing overnight. A Sybil farmer would need to fund real compute for every quill in the flock, and when hundreds of fresh identities attest each other in a sudden gale of cross-votes, the ledger correlation check flags the cluster and withholds weight until the work is proven independently.
